overview.description: An end-to-end autonomous trading system that ingests free alternative data sources (satellite imagery, aircraft tracking, seismic data, financial indicators) to detect geopolitical and real-world anomalies before prediction markets price them in, executing on Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated US event contract exchange. The system is grounded in backtested results: $500 grew to $7,778 across 16 trades (11 wins, 5 losses) over a 270-day backtest period, detecting the Oct 7 Gaza attack as an 11.1x thermal anomaly, the Kursk offensive 4 days before official confirmation, and Assad's fall 3 weeks early via escalating thermal signals. v3.0 integrates four convergent intelligence layers: (1) a multi-source anomaly detection engine using NASA FIRMS thermal data as the primary signal with 9 confirming sources forming a $0/month 10-source free data stack, (2) a Kalshi orderbook intelligence pipeline analyzing order flow patterns and volume anomalies, (3) a logic arbitrage engine that exploits causal event chains across Kalshi's structured contract categories before markets reprice downstream consequences, and (4) a Claude-based decision engine that synthesizes all signals into trade decisions with dynamic Kelly sizing. The Soros-archetype pattern (Magamyman: $800K deployed, 93% win rate on military strike predictions, CNN/Columbia Law School investigated) demonstrates that geopolitical information edges produce outsized returns -- the alternative data stack provides a legal, publicly available approximation of this edge. Edge decay analysis (BTC latency arbitrage compressed from 9.4s to 3.1s) informs strategy lifecycle management: FIRMS satellite data is early in its exploitation lifecycle, but signal durability must be actively monitored. The 4-6 hour FIRMS NRT publication delay constrains execution to swing-style positioning (hours to days), not high-frequency trading, targeting Kalshi contracts with multi-day resolution windows across geopolitics, conflict, sanctions, and military event categories.
objectives: Detect geopolitical anomalies 1-21 days before Kalshi markets price them in, using the 10-source free data stack anchored by NASA FIRMS satellite thermal data

Maintain a $0/month alternative data pipeline (9 of 10 sources require no API key) running a 40-second full scan cycle every 15 minutes, outperforming $24K/year Bloomberg Terminal for satellite-based conflict detection

Implement the anomaly detection statistical framework: 14-day rolling average baseline with 3x threshold, continuation bias filter (skip when 7-day baseline triples), and Fire Radiative Power (FRP in MW) severity grading

Execute logic arbitrage by mapping causal event chains across Kalshi's structured contract categories (politics -> economics -> geopolitical) and positioning on downstream contracts before market repricing

Map satellite and alternative data anomalies to specific Kalshi event categories: geopolitics (military action, regime change, conflict escalation), politics (sanctions, government policy), economics (CPI, GDP, Fed rate decisions influenced by conflict-driven commodity shocks)

Build a Claude-powered decision engine that cross-references all data sources, reasons about causal chains, estimates true probabilities, and outputs structured trade decisions with ~70% directional accuracy

Apply dynamic Kelly Criterion position sizing scaled by anomaly severity and confirmation count: quarter-Kelly ceiling, producing $41 losses on false alarms vs $470 gains on true signals through position size modulation
Analyze Kalshi orderbook data to detect institutional positioning patterns, volume anomalies, and price dislocations, compensating for the absence of on-chain wallet transparency

Monitor edge decay and signal compression: track exploitation lifecycle of FIRMS satellite edge, assess whether Kalshi's smaller US-only participant base compresses edges slower than larger retail platforms
Execute trades autonomously on Kalshi via REST API with configurable risk limits, achieving the backtested benchmark of positive EV across 16+ trades with 60%+ directional accuracy
Record complete market data (order books, fills, spreads) to enable statistically valid backtesting with minimum 1000 windows per strategy
constraints: All data sources must be free ($0/month total cost for the 10-source stack)

NASA FIRMS NRT data has ~3 hour processing delay; URT (Ultra Real-Time) available within ~60 seconds but with less coverage. The 4-6 hour publication delay means swing trading not HFT -- must target Kalshi contracts with multi-day resolution windows

Kalshi political/geopolitical markets may have variable liquidity; position sizes must be capped at 2% of market volume and respect Kalshi per-market position limits. Thinner order books than prior platforms may reduce strategy capacity

Claude API provides ~70% directional accuracy, which dynamic quarter-Kelly sizing must absorb. False alarm cost $41 (small position on weak signal); true signal made $470 (scaled position on strong signal)
Anomaly detection only works for FIRST spikes; continuation signals after baseline tripling must be filtered via the continuation bias mechanism (skip when 7-day baseline itself triples)

Sample size is inherently small for geopolitical events (7 major events over 16 months, 22 signals in the 270-day backtest); system must be treated as a proof of concept with real data until 50+ live signals accumulate

Data latency vs market speed mismatch is uncharacterized: if Kalshi geopolitical contracts fully reprice within 1-2 hours of news, FIRMS NRT signal may arrive too late. The window between FIRMS data availability and full market repricing on Kalshi requires empirical measurement

Kalshi does not expose individual trader positions or wallet data -- orderbook microstructure provides weaker signals than on-chain wallet analysis. Compensate by increasing weight on satellite/alternative data signals
System must operate on a 15-minute polling cycle with full pipeline executing in under 90-120 seconds

Full KYC required on Kalshi. CFTC regulation adds both legitimacy (legal US access) and scrutiny (regulatory sensitivity of geopolitical trading). Must stay clearly on the 'alternative data analysis' side of the legal boundary, not 'material non-public information'
Security: RSA-PSS per-request signing for Kalshi API, strong unique password, 2FA, secure PEM key storage. Start with minimal funds ($50-100). No blockchain wallets needed.

Edge decay is measurable and must be monitored: FIRMS satellite edge is early in lifecycle but the source material itself accelerates discovery. Counter-strategy is continuous discovery of new data sources and causal chains.
assumptions: NASA FIRMS API will remain free and accessible with MAP_KEY registration at firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov

OpenSky Network (free registered account, 4,000 credits/day), USGS, CoinGecko (free Demo API key), ExchangeRate API (free key), Alternative.me, and other free APIs will maintain current free-tier access
Kalshi will continue operating as a CFTC-regulated exchange with REST API access and USD cash settlement
Claude API (Anthropic) will remain available at current pricing (~$0.015/query for analysis)

Thermal anomaly patterns from satellite data correlate with geopolitical escalation events with sufficient lead time -- validated by 270-day backtest across Gaza (11x anomaly), Kursk (4 days early), Assad (3 weeks early)

Prediction markets are inefficient enough in pricing geopolitical events that a 3-6 hour NRT data delay still provides actionable edge, particularly on Kalshi contracts with multi-day resolution windows
Kalshi's structured contract categories (politics, economics, geopolitical) create exploitable causal chains where repricing delays in downstream contracts persist for minutes to hours
Kalshi's smaller, US-only participant base may produce more durable edges than larger platforms, though this is unvalidated
The $500 to $7,778 backtest result (16 trades, 270 days) is reproducible in live trading with realistic slippage, though the small trade count means high variance

components.name: DataIngestionLayer
components.description: Centralized data collection service polling all 10 alternative data sources on a 15-minute cycle. Handles API key management (NASA FIRMS MAP_KEY, OpenSky credentials, CoinGecko Demo key, ExchangeRate key), rate limiting, retry logic, and data persistence. Total cost: $0/month. Full cycle executes in ~40 seconds via async parallel polling. 9 of 10 sources require no API key.
responsibilities: Poll all 10 data sources every 15 minutes with async parallel requests
Normalize heterogeneous API responses into unified internal format
Handle rate limits, retries with exponential backoff, and graceful degradation on source failure
Persist all raw data to local storage for backtesting (DataRecorder integration)
Manage API credentials securely via .env (NASA MAP_KEY, OpenSky account, CoinGecko key, ExchangeRate key, Kalshi RSA key)

components.name: AnomalyDetectionEngine
components.description: Statistical anomaly detection framework processing all data sources through a deliberately simple but robust methodology: 14-day rolling average baseline per region per source, with 3x threshold triggering anomaly flags. This caught every major geopolitical event in the 270-day backtest. Sophistication comes from multi-source confirmation, not complex single-source models. Implements continuation bias filter to suppress signals where the baseline itself has tripled in the last 7 days, preventing bets on the 'new normal'. Fire Radiative Power (FRP in MW) adds severity dimension beyond binary fire count: distinguishes brushfire from bombardment from industrial explosion.
responsibilities: Compute 14-day rolling average baseline per region per data source
Flag anomalies exceeding configurable threshold (default 3x for FIRMS fire count)
Apply continuation bias filter: skip when 7-day baseline has tripled vs prior 7-day baseline
Grade severity using FRP (megawatts): brushfire vs bombardment vs industrial explosion
Generalize anomaly framework to all sources: seismic data, currency moves, flight pattern changes, volume spikes
Output structured anomaly records with magnitude ratio, peak FRP, coordinates, and timestamp
outputs: Anomaly records per region per source with magnitude, FRP, coordinates, timestamps, continuation flag

components.name: ConfirmationScorer
components.description: Computes composite tension score (0-100) by weighting each confirming data source. Higher scores indicate multi-source convergence. Only anomalies with confirmation_count >= 2 are passed to the decision engine. The power of the 10-source stack comes from cross-correlation: a FIRMS thermal spike confirmed by OpenSky military traffic and a RUB crash is qualitatively different from FIRMS alone.
responsibilities: Weight each triggered source according to configurable model (FIRMS 30, OpenSky 15, USGS 15, currency 10, VIX 10, gold 5, fear/greed 5, crypto 5, weather 5)
Compute normalized tension score 0-100
Enforce minimum 2-source confirmation before generating trade signals
Classify signal confidence: low (0-30), medium (31-50), high (51-75), critical (76-100)

components.name: KalshiOrderFlowAnalyzer
components.description: Extracts trading signals from Kalshi orderbook and market microstructure. Replaces the on-chain wallet intelligence from prior platform versions since Kalshi is not blockchain-based. Provides weaker but still useful signals via volume anomaly detection, price history analysis, spread dynamics, and cross-market correlation. Partially compensates for lack of individual trader position visibility.
responsibilities: Record full orderbook snapshots (bid/ask depth) for all monitored markets via REST and WebSocket
Detect volume anomalies: 3x+ above 14-day average on geopolitical contracts
Identify concentrated buying/selling: 80%+ of volume on one side in 1-hour windows
Track spread compression (50%+ narrowing from baseline) indicating informed flow
Detect cross-market correlations: volume spikes on multiple related contracts simultaneously
Analyze price momentum: 5%+ directional moves without corresponding news as early-mover signals
Map cross-market price movements to predict related contract repricing
inputs: Kalshi WebSocket orderbook deltas and fills

components.name: LogicArbitrageEngine
components.description: Exploits causal dependencies between events before Kalshi markets reprice downstream consequences. When event A triggers event B with high probability, positions on event B contracts while market still prices them at pre-A levels. Kalshi's structured categories (politics, economics, geopolitical) naturally create causal chains across contract types. Speed advantage measured in minutes to hours, accessible without HFT infrastructure. Example chain: sanctions announced -> currency crash -> regime instability -> military action probability increases.
responsibilities: Maintain a causal event graph mapping dependencies between Kalshi contract categories
Detect trigger events (upstream cause) and identify underpriced downstream consequence contracts
Estimate repricing delay between cause and consequence across Kalshi's fragmented markets
Integrate with Claude decision engine for causal chain reasoning that rule-based systems cannot express
Identify overpriced YES contracts on events that become impossible once prerequisite events resolve differently (Chinese dev NO bets pattern)
Track historical repricing timing data to build a systematic catalog of proven causal chains
outputs: Logic arbitrage trade opportunities with causal chain descriptions

components.name: KalshiEventCategoryMapper
components.description: Maps geopolitical anomaly signals to specific Kalshi contract categories and active markets. This is the critical bridge between satellite data and tradeable contracts. Kalshi categories with alt-data mapping: geopolitics (military action, regime change, conflict escalation), politics (sanctions triggers, election consequences, policy cascades), economics (Fed response to crisis, GDP impacts, trade disruption, CPI overshoot from conflict-driven commodity shocks). Also feeds the LogicArbitrageEngine with cross-category causal chain targets.
responsibilities: Map anomaly types to Kalshi categories: FIRMS thermal -> military action, conflict escalation; OpenSky aircraft -> military mobilization, evacuation; USGS seismic -> nuclear test, industrial catastrophe; Currency crashes -> sanctions, economic crisis; VIX + gold -> broad risk confirmation
Identify specific active markets matching each anomaly type with sufficient liquidity (>$5K open interest)
Verify contract resolution criteria match anomaly signal (Kalshi contracts may resolve on different criteria than expected)
Generate cross-category causal chain targets for logic arbitrage
Account for Kalshi's fee structure (1-7 cent settlement fees) in target market selection
inputs: Anomaly records with type and region
outputs: Ranked list of target Kalshi markets per anomaly

components.name: ClaudeDecisionEngine
components.description: Central trade decision brain receiving all signals and outputting structured JSON trade decisions. Replaces thousands of lines of rule-based correlation logic with natural language reasoning about causal relationships between heterogeneous signals. Approximately 70% directional accuracy on geopolitical signals -- sufficient for profitability with Kelly sizing. Critical for logic arbitrage: Claude reasons about causal chains (event A -> event B) that rule-based systems cannot express. Integration is 20-50 lines replacing 4,000+ lines of rule-based trading logic. Cost: ~$0.015/query via API.
responsibilities: Ingest anomaly data, tension scores, orderbook signals, logic arbitrage opportunities, and active Kalshi market data
Cross-reference signals across modalities: FIRMS thermal spike + RUB crash + VIX spike + OpenSky military traffic = high-confidence geopolitical trade
Reason about causal chains: anomaly -> political event -> economic impact -> specific Kalshi contract
Estimate true probabilities for Kalshi contract outcomes
Calculate edge vs current Kalshi market price (minimum 5% edge to trade)
Output structured JSON: action, ticker, probability estimate, edge, confidence, reasoning, recommended Kelly fraction, causal chain
Map geopolitical signals to specific Kalshi categories and identify contracts with sufficient liquidity
outputs: Structured trade decision JSON with action, ticker, probability, edge, confidence, reasoning, Kelly fraction, causal chain

components.name: PositionSizingEngine
components.description: Dynamic Kelly Criterion position sizing scaled by anomaly severity and confirmation count. Always uses quarter-Kelly (25% of full Kelly) as ceiling -- historical evidence shows full Kelly is emotionally destructive. Backtest results: 11x FIRMS anomaly + 6 confirming sources -> Kelly 50% of quarter allocation; random 3x blip + 1 source -> Kelly 3%. False alarm cost $41 (small position on weak signal); real signal made $470 (scaled position on strong signal). Asymmetry comes from position size modulation, not prediction accuracy.
responsibilities: Calculate base Kelly fraction: f* = (p * b - q) / b where b = (1 - P_market) / P_market
Apply quarter-Kelly ceiling (25% of full Kelly)
Scale by anomaly magnitude (min(magnitude/10, 1.0)) and confirmation count ratio
Enforce risk limits: max 15% single position, 50% portfolio exposure, 2% of market volume
Apply Kalshi per-market position limits as hard ceiling
Filter out trades with EV < 5%
Account for Kalshi settlement fees (1-7 cents per contract) in EV calculations
Account for Kalshi contract-specific liquidity depth in position sizing

components.name: ExecutionEngine
components.description: Handles trade execution on Kalshi via REST API with RSA-PSS per-request signing authentication. Supports dry-run mode (demo-api.kalshi.co) and live mode (api.elections.kalshi.com). Implements limit orders with slippage protection, automatic exit rules. Stateless auth: each request signed with private key, no login endpoint, no tokens, no refresh.
responsibilities: Authenticate via RSA-PSS per-request signing (KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE headers)
Place limit orders with 2% slippage tolerance
Monitor exit rules every 15-minute cycle: take-profit (+50%), stop-loss (-30%), time-stop (14 days)
Support batch operations (up to 20 orders per batch request)
Support order amendment (price/count changes without cancel+recreate)
Maintain dry-run and live mode separation
Connect to WebSocket for real-time fill and orderbook streaming

components.name: EdgeDecayMonitor
components.description: Tracks the exploitation lifecycle of each signal type to manage strategy durability. Edge decay is quantitatively measurable: BTC latency arbitrage compressed from 9.4 to 3.1 seconds (67% reduction), weather lag strategies show 83% win rate at 6-10 minutes that will inevitably compress, 73% of latency arb profits now go to sub-100ms bots. Every signal has a finite exploitable lifetime. FIRMS satellite data edge is early in lifecycle but source material itself accelerates discovery. Kalshi edges may be more durable than larger platforms due to smaller US-only participant base, but this is unvalidated.
responsibilities: Track signal-to-fill timing for each anomaly type over time
Detect compression in lead time (time between signal generation and market repricing)
Monitor false positive rate trends per signal type
Alert when edge appears to be compressing (lead time reduction >30% over 30-day window)
Recommend strategy rotation when edge approaches death phase
Compare edge durability between Kalshi and other platforms if data available
Track number of competing participants using similar signals (monitoring social media mentions, academic publications)
outputs: Edge health reports per signal type

components.name: DataRecorder
components.description: Records complete market microstructure data for valid backtesting. Critical design lesson: data completeness > strategy quality. Must record full order book depth, real spreads, actual fill behavior. Minimum 1000 windows per strategy for statistical confidence. Perfect execution assumption is fatal.
responsibilities: Record Kalshi orderbook snapshots at all price levels via REST and WebSocket
Record all trade fills with price, size, timestamp
Record all 10 alternative data source readings with timestamps
Record signal generation events with full context
Record execution records (order placed, fill price, slippage, partial fills)
Record Kalshi account balance and position snapshots
Maintain state recovery via last_run_state.json for crash resilience
outputs: Local JSON/Parquet files organized by date and market

components.name: AlertSystem
components.description: Real-time Telegram notification system covering anomaly detections, trade signals, executed trades, exit events, orderbook signals, edge decay warnings, and system health.
responsibilities: Send ANOMALY_DETECTED alerts: region, magnitude, FRP, confirming sources, tension score
Send TRADE_SIGNAL alerts: Kalshi ticker, price, edge, size, Claude reasoning, causal chain
Send TRADE_EXECUTED alerts: ticker, direction, contract count, fill price, slippage, USD cost
Send EXIT_TRIGGERED alerts: ticker, reason (TP/SL/time/settlement), PnL, hold duration
Send ORDERBOOK_SIGNAL alerts: volume anomaly or price momentum details
Send EDGE_DECAY_WARNING alerts: signal type, compression rate, recommended action
Send SYSTEM_HEALTH alerts: API failures, data gaps, pipeline latency, RSA key access errors
Rate limit: max 1 alert per type per 5 minutes

components.name: MonitoredRegions
components.description: Configurable list of geopolitical regions monitored by the anomaly detection engine. Each region defined by a bounding box (lat/lon) and associated Kalshi market categories. Default regions: Israel/Gaza, Ukraine/Kursk, Syria, Iran, Korean Peninsula, Taiwan Strait. All validated against the 270-day backtest (Gaza detected Oct 7 at 11.1x, Kursk detected 4 days early with 0-to-16 fire spike, Syria showed 3 weeks of escalating signal).
responsibilities: Define bounding boxes for all monitored geopolitical regions
Map each region to relevant Kalshi contract categories and example markets
Support dynamic region addition when new geopolitical hotspots emerge
Contextualize signal origin (e.g., Iran bbox western boundary captures Baghdad -- Claude must distinguish Iraqi vs Iranian activity)
outputs: Region bounding boxes for FIRMS/OpenSky queries

architecture.data_flow: 15-minute cycle: (1) DataIngestionLayer polls all 10 sources across all monitored regions in ~40 seconds via async parallel requests -> (2) AnomalyDetectionEngine computes 14-day rolling baselines, flags anomalies at 3x threshold, applies continuation bias filter, grades FRP severity -> (3) ConfirmationScorer computes composite tension score (0-100), filters for minimum 2 confirming sources -> (4) KalshiOrderFlowAnalyzer provides orderbook signals: volume anomalies, price momentum, spread compression from Kalshi market data -> (5) KalshiEventCategoryMapper identifies which Kalshi contract categories and specific active markets match the detected anomaly type -> (6) LogicArbitrageEngine identifies causal chain opportunities: upstream trigger events with underpriced downstream consequence contracts -> (7) ClaudeDecisionEngine receives anomalies + scores + orderbook signals + category mapping + logic arbitrage opportunities + active markets, outputs structured trade decision JSON with causal chain reasoning -> (8) PositionSizingEngine calculates dynamic quarter-Kelly position scaled by anomaly magnitude and confirmation count, capped by Kalshi position limits and liquidity -> (9) ExecutionEngine places limit order on Kalshi via REST API (or logs dry-run on demo API) -> (10) AlertSystem sends Telegram notification with full context -> (11) DataRecorder logs all inputs, decisions, and executions -> (12) EdgeDecayMonitor tracks signal-to-fill timing and compression trends. Exit monitoring runs every cycle checking open positions against TP/SL/time-stop rules.

risks.description: Small sample size for geopolitical events: 7 major events over 16 months, 22 signals in 270-day backtest, only 16 trades generating the $500-to-$7,778 result. High variance is inherent.
risks.mitigation: Treat system as proof-of-concept with real data until 50+ live signals accumulate. Run extended dry-run periods. Supplement with non-geopolitical anomaly markets (economic indicators, climate events) to increase signal count. Kalshi's broader contract categories (economics, climate) provide more trading opportunities beyond pure geopolitical events.

risks.description: Data latency vs market speed mismatch: FIRMS NRT has ~3 hour delay, and no empirical data exists on how quickly Kalshi geopolitical contracts reprice after news breaks. If Kalshi markets fully reprice within 1-2 hours, FIRMS NRT signal arrives too late.
risks.mitigation: Evaluate FIRMS URT (Ultra Real-Time, ~60 second delay) for time-critical regions. Cross-reference with real-time sources (OpenSky, financial indicators) that update faster. Empirically measure FIRMS-to-Kalshi repricing window in Phase 5. Target contracts with multi-day resolution windows where 3-6 hour delays are acceptable. Accept that some events will be missed.

risks.description: Edge decay and signal compression: FIRMS satellite edge is early in exploitation lifecycle but source material accelerates discovery. Every signal has finite exploitable lifetime (BTC arb compressed 9.4s to 3.1s, 67% reduction).
risks.mitigation: EdgeDecayMonitor tracks signal-to-fill timing compression. Kalshi's smaller US-only participant base may slow compression vs larger platforms. Counter-strategy: continuously discover new data sources and causal chains rather than defending a single edge. Monitor social media and academic publications for competing usage of FIRMS data.

risks.description: Kalshi geopolitical/political market liquidity may be thin: Kalshi has lower liquidity than larger prediction market platforms, and $2K orders may move price 3-5% on thinly traded contracts.
risks.mitigation: Hard cap position size at 2% of market volume. Respect Kalshi per-market position limits. Use limit orders with tight slippage tolerance. Prefer markets with meaningful open interest (>$5K). Consider economics contracts (CPI, Fed rate) as higher-liquidity alternatives still influenced by geopolitical events.

risks.description: Regulatory sensitivity of geopolitical trading on Kalshi: CFTC regulation adds legitimacy but also scrutiny. CNN-style investigations of informed geopolitical trading could affect Kalshi participants. The legal boundary between 'alternative data analysis' and 'material non-public information' in the context of government satellite feeds is untested.
risks.mitigation: All data sources are free, publicly available, and legal. NASA FIRMS is a public government feed -- using it is alternative data analysis, not insider trading. Maintain full audit trail of signal generation and decision process. Stay clearly on the public data side. Monitor CFTC regulatory filings and Kalshi announcements.

risks.description: Kalshi category mapping gaps: which specific Kalshi event categories and contract types map best to satellite thermal anomaly signals has not been empirically validated. FIRMS detects conflict and catastrophe, but Kalshi's exact contract taxonomy, resolution criteria, and historical liquidity per category are uncharacterized.
risks.mitigation: Phase 2 builds the KalshiEventCategoryMapper with explicit anomaly-to-category mapping rules. Phase 5 validates mappings against historical contract resolutions. Start with obvious mappings (FIRMS + Middle East -> military action contracts) and expand based on empirical results.

risks.description: False positive anomaly signals: wildfires, agricultural burns, industrial activity, and seasonal patterns generate FIRMS detections that are not geopolitical events.
risks.mitigation: Multi-source confirmation requirement (minimum 2 sources). Claude cross-references anomaly context with known seasonal patterns. Continuation bias filter suppresses signals in elevated regions. FRP severity grading helps distinguish military bombardment from brush fires. Conservative 3x threshold adjustable per region.

risks.description: Claude directional accuracy degradation or API changes affecting the ~70% accuracy baseline.
risks.mitigation: Quarter-Kelly sizing absorbs 30% wrong calls. Log all Claude decisions and outcomes. Monitor rolling accuracy. Pause live trading if accuracy drops below 55%. Keep prompt template versioned. The $41 loss on false alarms vs $470 gain on true signals shows the system is profitable even with significant error rate.

risks.description: Reduced signal transparency vs on-chain platforms: Kalshi does not expose individual trader positions or wallet data, weakening the behavioral analysis intelligence layer.
risks.mitigation: Accept KalshiOrderFlowAnalyzer provides weaker signals than on-chain wallet analysis. Compensate by: (1) increasing weight on satellite/alternative data which remains equally strong, (2) leveraging Kalshi's stronger geopolitical contract coverage for more direct market targets, (3) using orderbook microstructure as probabilistic not deterministic signals. The logic arbitrage and causal chain approaches are new edges that did not exist on prior platforms.

risks.description: Cross-validation gap: no analysis exists of whether FIRMS-detected events also show unusual Kalshi order activity. Satellite signals and orderbook signals may be redundant rather than complementary.
risks.mitigation: Phase 5 includes explicit cross-validation between satellite anomaly approach and orderbook behavioral analysis. Determine empirically whether signals are redundant or complementary. Adjust confirmation weights based on findings.

risks.description: Overfitting anomaly thresholds and confirmation weights to the limited historical event set (Gaza, Kursk, Syria).
risks.mitigation: Use walk-forward validation, not static backtest optimization. Keep parameter count minimal (3x threshold is one number, not a curve-fitted model). Track performance on events not in training set. The deliberate simplicity of the anomaly detection framework (14-day rolling average, 3x threshold) is a feature that resists overfitting.

risks.description: Kalshi API changes, rate limit adjustments, or fee structure changes affecting system operation.
risks.mitigation: Pin API version (v2). Monitor Kalshi API changelog. Implement graceful degradation for API failures. Maintain abstraction layer between trading logic and API client. Account for settlement fees (1-7 cents) in EV calculations with buffer.

risks.description: Logic arbitrage causal chain framework lacks systematic catalog: currently relies on ad-hoc reasoning rather than a validated database of proven political/geopolitical causal chains with historical repricing timing.
risks.mitigation: Phase 5 builds the systematic catalog. Claude's causal reasoning capability partially compensates in the interim. Start with well-known chains (conflict -> oil -> CPI -> Fed rate) and expand as empirical data accumulates. Track repricing delays per chain type.

success_criteria: Generates trade signal within 24 hours of market price moving >5 cents on a Kalshi geopolitical/political contract, on 80%+ of such movements exceeding 10 cents

Reproduces backtested results: detects Oct 7 (11.1x anomaly), Kursk (4 days early), Assad (3 weeks early) with <2 hour timing variance from original analysis and maps each to corresponding Kalshi contract price movements
False positive rate below 40% for multi-source confirmed signals (confirmation_count >= 3)

Live trading achieves positive expected value over a rolling 30-trade window with at least 60% directional accuracy on anomaly-triggered trades, benchmarked against the backtest $500-to-$7,778 trajectory

Position sizing prevents any single trade loss from exceeding 5% of total bankroll through quarter-Kelly, liquidity caps, and Kalshi position limits. False alarms cost ~$41 (weak signal, small position); true signals return ~$470 (strong signal, scaled position)
Full pipeline executes in under 90-120 seconds per 15-minute cycle (40-second data ingestion + anomaly detection + Claude decision at 2-10s + order placement)
Data recorder achieves 99%+ uptime capturing complete orderbook and trade data for all monitored Kalshi markets
KalshiEventCategoryMapper successfully links 90%+ of detected geopolitical anomalies to at least one active Kalshi market with >$5K open interest
Logic arbitrage engine identifies at least 3 causal chain opportunities per month across Kalshi contract categories with measurable repricing delays
EdgeDecayMonitor tracks signal compression and provides 30-day advance warning before an edge becomes unprofitable
Cross-validation in Phase 5 empirically determines whether satellite and orderbook signals are redundant or complementary, with documented findings
Data latency measurement in Phase 5 empirically characterizes the FIRMS-to-Kalshi repricing window for at least 5 event types
Telegram alerts deliver within 10 seconds of signal generation with complete decision context including causal chain
System runs 30+ consecutive days in dry-run mode (Kalshi demo API) without data gaps, crashes, or missed cycles before live capital deployment

notes: v3.0 integrates insights from the knowledge overview (overview_id: 5ea2845d) synthesizing 4 additional research items covering NASA FIRMS thermal anomaly detection, Soros-archetype information edges, logic arbitrage via causal chains, wallet behavioral analysis, and edge decay quantification. Key changes from v2.1: (1) New LogicArbitrageEngine component exploiting causal event chain repricing delays across Kalshi's structured contract categories -- minutes-to-hours speed advantage accessible without HFT infrastructure. (2) New EdgeDecayMonitor component tracking signal lifecycle and compression, informed by quantified BTC lag decay (9.4s to 3.1s) and weather lag patterns (83% win rate, 6-10 minute leads). (3) Grounded backtest numbers throughout: $500 to $7,778 on 16 trades (11W/5L), 270-day period, Oct 7 detected as 11.1x anomaly (69 fires vs 6.4 baseline, 34 MW max FRP), Kursk 4 days early (0 to 16 fires), Assad 3 weeks early. (4) Soros-archetype context: Magamyman wallet pattern ($800K deployed, 93% win rate on military strikes, CNN/Columbia Law School investigated) demonstrates the magnitude of geopolitical information edges -- the alternative data stack provides a legal, publicly available approximation. (5) Knowledge gaps explicitly addressed as risks and Phase 5 deliverables: Kalshi category mapping validation, data latency vs market speed empirical measurement, cross-validation between satellite and orderbook approaches, systematic causal chain catalog construction. (6) All prior platform references replaced with Kalshi equivalents. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated US exchange with USD cash settlement, RSA-PSS API authentication, and structured event categories that provide more direct correlation with geopolitical signals than prior platforms. (7) Regulatory considerations expanded: CFTC oversight, legal boundary between alternative data analysis and material non-public information, precedent from CNN investigations of geopolitical prediction market trading. (8) 4-6 hour FIRMS delay constraint explicitly positioned as swing trading not HFT throughout, targeting multi-day resolution contracts. (9) $0/month total data cost (9 of 10 sources keyless) positioned against $24K/year Bloomberg Terminal. The fundamental insight remains unchanged: the edge is not in strategy sophistication but in data sources nobody else is monitoring (satellite thermal anomalies) combined with mathematical discipline (dynamic quarter-Kelly) and automation (Claude decision engine with causal chain reasoning).
